name: Should you choose tile or acrylic for a tub-to-shower conversion?

mainEntity.name: Should homeowners choose a tiled shower or an acrylic wall system for a tub-to-shower conversion?
mainEntity.text: Should homeowners choose a tiled shower or an acrylic wall system for a tub-to-shower conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tile and acrylic solve different problems. Tile is best when the homeowner wants a custom look, more design options, and a higher-end finish. It can match a luxury remodel well, but it requires excellent waterproofing and regular grout maintenance. Acrylic or other solid wall systems are often faster to install, easier to clean, and less expensive than a fully tiled shower. They are a strong option when low maintenance is the top priority. For many Los Angeles-area homeowners, the decision comes down to budget, style, and how much upkeep they want long term. Tile can add value in design-forward homes, while acrylic can be more practical for secondary bathrooms or accessibility upgrades. The key question is not which material is universally better, but which one fits the project goals. Ask the contractor to show samples, explain warranty coverage, and clarify what maintenance the finished shower will need over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tile offers more design flexibility and a custom look, while acrylic is usually faster to install and easier to maintain. Tile generally costs more and depends heavily on proper waterproofing and grout care, while acrylic is simpler and often lower maintenance.
